item.title: Swedish word of the day: nyckelpiga
item.description: These little red and black insects pop up in gardens and fields all across Sweden during the spring and summer. But where does their name come from?

item.title: What happens if your Swedish citizenship application is rejected?
item.description: Has your Swedish citizenship application been denied, despite you meeting all the requirements? Here are your next steps, as well as how to appeal if you think the Migration Agency has made a mistake.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Man killed in Eskilstuna in year's first fatal shooting, Social Democrats oppose welfare restrictions for immigrants, and other news from Sweden on Tuesday.

item.title: Swedish lawyers declare plan to revoke permanent residencies 'illegal'
item.description: More than 35 of Sweden's top lawyers have written a joint article declaring a government proposal to strip permanent residency from up to 180,000 to be illegal, declaring it as, "simply put, a stupid proposal".

item.title: Three years after The Local, Sweden wakes up to teen deportations
item.description: The Local has been writing about teen deportations for years. Why did it take everyone else so long to catch up?

item.title: EU's EES biometric passport checks catch 4,000 over-stayers in first 4 months
item.description: One of the stated aims of the EU's new EES system of biometric passport checks is to catch people who 'over-stay' the 90-day limit, and 4,000 of those have been caught in the first months of its implementation, according to an EU official.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: dum
item.description: Despite its similarity to the English word dumb, dum doesn’t mean exactly the same thing in Swedish.

item.title: Law intended to stop Sweden's teen deportations 'likely to increase them'
item.description: The proposed law that Sweden's migration minister claims will end teen deportations is likely instead to lead to a sharp rise in the number of children of work permit holders ordered to leave the country, one of Sweden's top immigration lawyers has told The Local.

item.title: When is Sweden's parliament set to vote on new migration laws?
item.description: Sweden's government is currently racing to get some of the most important laws drawn up as part of its "paradigm shift on migration" passed by parliament before the election in September. Here is a list of when the key votes are set to take place.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
item.description: Two thirds of Tidö Agreement fulfilled, Swedish politicians laud Ukraine on four-year anniversary, and more news from Sweden on Wednesday.
